data.gender_notes: Elita is used as a unisex name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Elita is derived from the Sanskrit word 'Elita', which means 'Goddess of Light'. In Hindu mythology, Elita is the goddess of knowledge, wisdom, and the sun. She is often depicted holding a lotus flower or a book, symbolizing knowledge and learning. The name Elita carries the meaning “Goddess of Light” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Elita usually hope their child will grow to embody goddess of light and live with faith, good character and purpose.

historical_references.reference: Elita, also known as Ilalita or Elattarai, was a Jaina princess and the wife of Mahavira, the last Tirthankara of Jainism. She is considered an ideal Jaina wife and is revered for her devotion, faith and ascetic practices.

Elita Devi, a queen of the Mughal Emperor Shah Jahan, was known for her beauty, grace and piety. She was the mother of Prince Dara Shikoh, the eldest son of Shah Jahan. She is remembered for her devotion to the Sufi saint Salim Chishti and her efforts to spread the message of Sufism in the Mughal court.
